target: shape (PATO_0000052) with values obovate (PATO_0001936) and oblong (PATO_0000946), read as a range between the two
fix: A hyphenated shape like 'obovate-oblong' means a shape between the two. Keep both halves as a range from one to the other. Do not keep only the last word.
reason: The flora says the sepals are between obovate and oblong. The annotation keeps only 'oblong' and drops 'obovate'.
'Sepals ... 5–6 mm' is the sepal length.
The leaf blades range from oblanceolate to lanceolate, and the ids match these words.
'Synflorescence ... ± spikelike' means the inflorescence is roughly spike-like, and '±' becomes 'approximately'.

fix: 'pubescents-hirsutes' could also add hirsute, read as a range from pubescent to hirsute. The rachis needs its own record.
reason: The French says the petiole (and rachis) is ± pubescent to hirsute. 'Approximately pubescent' on the petiole holds.

target: position: the smallest sepal ('le plus petit'); value qualifier: approximately
fix: 'le plus grand ... le plus petit' (the largest ... the smallest) names one member of an unequal set. That position has to be kept, or the size is wrongly given to all sepals.
reason: Only the smallest sepal is about 2 mm across. The largest is about 5 mm long. Without the position, the record says all sepals are 2 mm across.
'Fleurs ... de 1 cm de large' is the flower width, 1 cm.

target: a relation to another part: stem height at most 1/5 of whole-plant (PO_0000003) height, with no absolute number
fix: A fraction of another part ('up to 1/5 height of plant') is a relation between two parts, not a size. The parser turned it into a number in a made-up unit.
reason: The flora gives only a share of the plant's height. The 'up to 2 cm' with source unit dm is not in the text.

fix: 'not seen' and 'not known' mean the part was never observed. They do not mean it is absent. Such statements should give no presence record.
reason: The authors did not see fruit. The flora does not say the plant has no fruit.

fix: The more exact PO class involucral bract (PO_0009045) exists and should be used for 'bractées involucrales'.
reason: There are 1–2 involucral bracts. 'bract' is a broader class but not false.

fix: With 'rarely present' following, a frequency qualifier 'usually' should be added.
reason: The petals are absent. The rare exception does not make the main statement wrong.
'Petals lanceolate'.
'many flowered' inflorescences: many flowers are present in the inflorescence. This is pattern 13 (indefinite count).

fix: In a compound-leaf description, 'blades' after 'leaflets ...; petiolule ...;' means the leaflet blades, not the whole leaf.
reason: The subleathery blades are the leaflets' blades. 'Approximately coriaceous' as the reading of 'subleathery' is fine.
'Spikelets densely arranged' means the spikelets are crowded.
The capsule opens by 2 valves, so there are 2 fruit valves.

target: position: upper cells of the leaf (the leaf's distal region)
fix: When 'upper cells' and 'basal cells' are described separately in a moss leaf, the position has to be kept with the cell record.
reason: Only the upper leaf cells are mammillose. The basal cells are described differently, so without the position the record covers all leaf cells.
'Mature fruit dry': the stage is mature and the fruit is dry.

fix: 'glaucous' is a waxy bloom on the surface, not the colour green. Map it to PATO glaucous.
reason: The statement says 'somewhat glaucous'. The green colour comes from 'pale green', which is a different statement.

target: the apex of the lateral lobes of the lip (lip lobe, apex position)
fix: 'apex ...' after 'lateral lobes ..., ...' is said of the lateral lobes' apex, not of the whole lip. 'obtuse-truncate' should also keep obtuse.
reason: The flora gives the apex shape of the lip's lateral lobes. The lip as a whole is 3-lobed, not truncate or acute.

fix: 'not known' means the part was never observed. It does not mean it is absent. Such statements should give no presence record.
reason: The capsule is unknown, not missing.

fix: The position (abaxial corners of the furrows) could be added, but it is not needed for the statement to be true.
reason: A few sclerenchyma strands are present.

fix: '(mostly n)' after a range gives the usual value inside the range. It is not a frequency qualifier on the whole range.
reason: 'Usually' belongs to 3, not to the range 1–4.
'Styles ... shorter than stamens'.

fix: In FNA, 'Herbs/Shrubs a × b dm' gives height × width (spread). The second number is width, not length.
reason: The plants are 0.2–1 dm tall and 0.5–2 dm across. The 5–20 cm range is the spread, not a length.
'Panicles ... many flowered': many flowers in the inflorescence.
The blades are linear or filiform.
'Leaves ... 1–1.5 cm × 0.5–0.8 mm': the length is 1–1.5 cm.

fix: 'Stems: submersed ...; emersed ...' gives each state its own measurement. The state word in front of the measurement belongs in the state slot.
reason: Only the emersed stems are 10–30(–45) cm. Submersed stems reach 60 cm, so without the state the record is false.
